game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
subject: Sheik / Princess Zelda
reading_summary: Critics and fans have read Zelda's presentation as Sheik as transgender, gender-ambiguous, or a disruption of the gender binary.
counterevidence: A Nintendo representative described Sheik as a woman and as Zelda in a different outfit. This record documents the reading and debate; it does not classify Sheik or Zelda as a transgender character.
notes: The archive labels the case queerly read or rumored rather than confirmed representation.

game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Majora’s Mask
subject: Tingle
reading_summary: Fans and critics have speculated that Tingle may be gay, often through readings of his camp presentation and gender expression.
counterevidence: Nintendo stated that Tingle was not intended to be a gay character. Mannerisms and presentation alone are not evidence of sexual orientation.
notes: Preserved as reception history and not counted as a gay character record.

subject: Link (series incarnations)
reading_summary: Several articles have proposed that Link, or particular incarnations of Link, could be gay.
counterevidence: The archive describes the arguments as inconclusive, and the games do not establish a fixed sexual orientation shared by Link's different incarnations.
notes: The subject spans distinct incarnations and is therefore unsuitable for a canonical character-identity row.

subject: Alfred Ashford
reading_summary: Alfred impersonates his absent twin sister Alexia, adopts a second persona bearing her identity, and wears her clothing. This presentation has been catalogued through cross-dressing, gender-nonconformity, and transphobic-coding lenses.
counterevidence: The story frames the presentation as impersonation connected to Alfred's deteriorating mental state and relationship with Alexia; it does not identify Alfred as transgender. Clothing, disguise, and a second persona do not by themselves establish gender identity.
notes: Retained as a historically relevant queer reading and example of potentially stigmatizing horror coding. Alfred is not counted as a confirmed transgender character in Press Q analytics.

subject: Morpheus Duvall
reading_summary: Morpheus uses a virus that transforms his body into a Tyrant form described by some sources as a female version of himself. This transformation has generated implicit-transgender and gender-nonconforming readings.
counterevidence: The game presents the bodily change as a viral mutation and does not explicitly identify Morpheus as transgender or state a changed gender identity. A feminized monster form is not sufficient evidence of a canonical trans identity.
notes: Recorded to document reception, gendered body-horror imagery, and possible transphobic coding without converting the interpretation into a confirmed character record.

subject: Electro
reading_summary: Some fans have read Electro as bisexual, and the interpretation has circulated alongside lists of LGBTQ+ Marvel characters in games.
counterevidence: The archive describes the claim as suspected and cites a fan-forum discussion rather than canonical game text, creator confirmation, or a supported Marvel identity. Repeated appearances in games do not establish sexual orientation.
notes: Preserved as reception history with low confidence in the documentation base. Electro is not counted as a confirmed bisexual character.

subject: Iron Man / Captain America
reading_summary: Iron Man dialogue alludes to the large body of fan fiction that pairs him romantically or sexually with Captain America, making same-gender fan interpretation visible inside the game.
counterevidence: The dialogue references fan culture; it does not establish Iron Man and Captain America as a canonical couple or confirm either character's sexual orientation.
notes: Recorded as an intertextual acknowledgment of queer fan practices rather than as two confirmed queer-character records.
